correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the operator span from the Weyl basis: conjugation diagonalizes by characters, so the span dimension is exactly the cardinality of the union of nonzero ambiguity coordinates. A two-point support contributes only translation rows 0 and ±d, giving the universal upper bound. The displayed unequal-amplitude windows make all coordinates on the selected rows nonzero; the even antipodal phase makes both parity classes nonzero. These arguments cover all \(N\ge2\) and \(s\ge1\). The bundled verifier independently checks ambiguity supports, direct projector ranks in small dimensions, and exhaustive support-pair row coverage.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete sharp resource tradeoff, not merely a feasibility example: for every dimension and every number of exactly two-sparse windows it determines the largest possible operator span and therefore the exact tomography threshold. Two-sparse windows are the minimal nontrivial spatial support, so the capacity curve quantifies how much full Gabor covariance can compensate for extreme window sparsity. The even-dimensional antipodal resonance is handled explicitly rather than hidden in a genericity argument.
